governed_construct: A module specifier in real code that refers to a project-local module: the string-literal source of an import declaration (including import type), an export ... from / export * from declaration, a dynamic import() call, or a require() call, whose specifier is either relative ('./', '../') or a path-mapped alias ('@/...'). Bare package specifiers (e.g. 'react', 'zod', '@scope/pkg') are not instances. Specifiers mentioned only in comments or string literals that are not import/require sources are not instances.
interpretation: The rule asks that local modules be imported through the tsconfig path mapping (e.g. '@/lib/prisma') rather than via relative paths. 'When possible' is read as: whenever the import crosses into a parent directory, an alias is possible and preferred, so any project-local specifier beginning with '../' is VIOLATED; an alias specifier ('@/...') conforms, and a same-directory './' specifier is tolerated as conforming because co-located sibling imports are the common exception where an alias adds nothing. A file is SATISFIED if it has at least one project-local import/export-from/require/dynamic-import source and none starts with '../'; VIOLATED if any one does; NOT_APPLICABLE if it imports only external packages or nothing at all. Commented-out imports and import-looking text inside ordinary string literals are ignored, which is why a regex over source text is unsound and the rule is T2 (a syntax query over ImportDeclaration/ExportDeclaration/CallExpression module-specifier nodes).
